bullets.title: Fed expected to hold; December hike to 4.25% priced, 10Y near 5%
bullets.body: Consensus across multiple desks has the FOMC holding this week with possible hawkish dissents; market pricing a December hike to 4.25% then a pause. The 10Y yield is trading around 4.97-5.00%, with Hedgeye flagging a UST 10Y range of 4.92-5.24% and JPM noting equities can tolerate 5.5-6.0% yields if AI productivity supports higher multiples.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle re-engaged; hyperscaler earnings this week are the key catalyst
bullets.body: JPM and UBS both flag a positioning washout in semis (net exposure at 17th percentile) that sets up a squeeze if AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, and INTC confirm capex this week. Tech mega-cap positioning collapsed from the 85th to 33rd percentile in early October; desks expect ~50% Q3 growth needed to sustain re-engagement.

bullets.title: META prices ~$97.5B equity offering; NVDA invests $3B as cornerstone
bullets.body: Meta upsized its equity offering to ~$97.5B at $625/share, with Nvidia investing $3B and AMD and AVGO also participating. The raise is intended to fund AI infrastructure capex that analysts estimate at $95B+ through 2028, which OPCO flags will lower 2027/28 EPS estimates 14-15% below Street and increase share count ~4%.

bullets.title: AVGO backstops $63B Anthropic chip financing — largest-ever AI infrastructure debt deal
bullets.body: Broadcom finalized a $63B, five-year debt financing package via an SPV with BofA, Blackstone, Citi, and Morgan Stanley to fund Anthropic's TPU purchases; CEO Tan negotiated higher rates and guarantees to protect lenders. The deal is being read as easing AI financing concerns and follows Meta's $95B equity raise and SpaceX's $40B debt raise.

bullets.title: Semiconductor ETFs log record ~$12.7B inflows as funds buy AI dip
bullets.body: Investors aggressively bought semiconductor ETF dips with record inflows: SOXX +$6.5B, SOXL +$2.8B, SMH +$2.6B. Hedge funds had rotated net selling from semis into hyperscalers, leaving AI net exposure at the 17th percentile — a setup that creates short-squeeze risk if earnings beat.

bullets.title: Anthropic S-1: $800B+ compute commitments, IPO valuation ~$1.5T vs. $2T expectations
bullets.body: Anthropic's H1 operating loss narrowed to ~$693M from $2.1B, but faces >$800B in noncancelable compute commitments (MSFT $44.9B+, GOOGL ~$114.5B+, AMZN $110B+, AVGO ~$161.2B). IPO valuation expected ~$1.5T; 48% of H1 revenue derived from hyperscaler cloud marketplaces, raising strategic-dependence concerns; Kedrosky views IPO timing as opportunistic before capital-intensive transition weakens financials.

bullets.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra at 50% lower cost — pricing war intensifies
bullets.body: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra at up to 50% lower cost per token than its predecessor, directly pressuring Anthropic's pricing model. Multiple desks flag this as intensifying competitive dynamics across the AI model layer.

bullets.title: Global data center capacity to grow 23% CAGR to ~316 GW by 2030; power is the binding constraint
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley projects global DC IT capacity reaching 316 GW by 2030E (+23% CAGR), with a 49 GW utility power shortfall expected by 2028 (demand 327 GW vs. supply 278 GW). Building cost inflation is trending >10% YoY; AI-related debt issuance is running at 2.2x last year's pace; contract pricing rose 11% YoY with 43% of capacity pre-leased globally. EQIX is named MS top pick at $1,250 PT.

bullets.title: Earnings reaction asymmetry: beats and misses both outperforming by 70bps — historic reversal
bullets.body: JPM desk flags that companies beating EPS are outperforming by only 70bps the following day, while misses are also outperforming by 70bps — a historic reversal suggesting the market is looking through near-term results toward forward guidance and AI capex confirmation.

bullets.title: Asia hedge fund AI unwind accelerating: Asia L/S funds down 8.9% MTD, net allocation cut 289bps
bullets.body: Goldman prime data shows Asia fundamental L/S managers down 8.9% MTD (China-focused -10.9%), driven by AI exposure losses beyond China. Taiwan, Korea, and Japan led selling flows; Info Tech remains 14.2% overweight vs. MXAP but net sold MTD. Net Asia allocation declined 289bps to 27.3%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 technicals: 4.5% max drawdown vs. 13.8% midterm avg suggests limited post-election upside
bullets.body: Multiple sources note the S&P 500's maximum drawdown this cycle is only ~4.5% vs. the 13.8% historical midterm average, raising concern that a post-election rally may disappoint. Hedgeye targets potential downside toward ~7,300; CTA equity exposure is at the 11th percentile with risk-control at 93rd percentile — a 2% S&P decline estimated to trigger ~$155B in systematic selling.

bullets.title: Hedgeye bearish cross-asset: oil at $116, QQQ trend bearish, Bitcoin breaking down
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags Brent crude at new cycle highs near $116, long USD at new quad-2 highs, and China Shanghai Composite down 6.1% over the last month to stagflation lows. QQQ is assigned a bearish trend signal; Bitcoin shows a 'textbook breakdown.' October CPI is expected to accelerate; December is called the last obvious monthly quad-2 print.

bullets.title: Chase spend decelerated to 5.8% YoY in Oct MTD vs. 6.8% in September; energy inflation is regressive
bullets.body: JPM Chase spending data shows October MTD deceleration to 5.8% YoY (vs. 6.8% September), with discretionary slowing to 5.4% from 6.9%. Energy spend is up 25.9% YoY, creating meaningful regressive pressure on lower- and middle-income consumers.

bullets.title: B-CCC credit spread near 8% creating unusual disconnect with equities only ~2% below highs
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags the B-to-CCC credit spread near 8%, a level historically associated with substantially larger equity drawdowns — an unusual disconnect given the S&P 500 is only ~2% below all-time highs. French sovereign spreads are also approaching 2010-12 European debt crisis levels amid political gridlock.

bullets.title: MSFT offers voluntary buyouts to ~60,000 employees to redirect spending toward AI
bullets.body: Microsoft announced voluntary buyout offers to approximately 60,000 employees as the company reallocates resources toward AI investment. This follows the broader trend of hyperscalers concentrating headcount and capex around AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: TSMC plans 20% CoWoS price increase — AI packaging inflation accelerating
bullets.body: TSMC is reportedly planning to raise CoWoS advanced packaging prices by up to 20%, adding to AI infrastructure cost inflation. This follows TSMC's prior CoWoS pricing increases and will flow through to AI accelerator customers across the hyperscaler and custom ASIC supply chain.

bullets.title: Key earnings this week: GOOGL, MSFT, NOW (Wed); AMZN, INTC, PINS (Thu); AAPL (Mon Nov 2)
bullets.body: Major tech earnings are concentrated Wed-Thu: Alphabet ($3.02 EPS est, $127.94B rev), Microsoft ($4.71, $90.62B), ServiceNow ($1.02, $4.09B) on Wednesday; Amazon ($1.97, $202.24B), Intel ($0.41, $16.53B) on Thursday. Apple ($1.99, $113.39B) and Shopify ($0.47) report November 2-3. Hyperscaler capex commentary is the primary focus.

bullets.title: Higher-for-longer rate regime: asset-sensitive Financials win; housing, select Utilities lose
bullets.body: JPM outlines the rate-regime playbook: higher-for-longer benefits asset-sensitive Financials; losers include refinancing-dependent housing, select Utilities needing rate relief; rate-agnostic areas include recurring software/cyber/payments and data centers. The framework matters as December hike odds remain elevated and the 10Y approaches 5%.

bullets.title: DASH in advanced talks to acquire CART for ~$17B; deal primarily equity with ~80M share dilution
bullets.body: Multiple sources confirm DoorDash is in advanced/exclusive talks to acquire Instacart at ~$17B, with a deal possible this week. The structure is primarily equity (~80M shares dilution); analysts model ~$100M revenue and ~$100M EBITDA synergies, valuing post-deal DASH at ~11x 2028E EBITDA. Regulatory scrutiny and strategic rationale are the key investor debates.

bullets.title: Open-weight models now 72% of token usage; questions mount on AI economic capture
bullets.body: With open-weight models representing 72% of token usage despite 27x token usage growth since November, multiple desks are raising questions about who ultimately captures AI economics. This dynamic is cited as a risk for model vendors and a tailwind for infrastructure/compute plays.
